identity.name: Charaf Achir
identity.positioning: Applied-AI engineer focused on taking GenAI systems from prototype to production.
identity.story: I turn ideas into applied AI: conversational systems, computer vision, and the occasional experiment that makes you smile.

availability.note: Open to conversations sooner and to a permanent role from September 2026.

experience.summary: Builds GenAI for LCP, the Amadeus loyalty platform. Built the configuration-chatbot proof of concept independently, helped establish the OctoMind team, and now works on Member Insight, the chatbot, and technical documentation for the AI stack.
Built and deployed client-facing and staff-facing assistants, including incoming-user qualification and quantitative portfolio analysis.

education.details: In progress alongside the Amadeus apprenticeship. Written work includes a professional thesis on AI-native decision systems and an apprenticeship experience report.
Master level, top 10%, with an exchange semester at KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm.

distinctions: Winner, HTE GeNiUS hackathon in Italy
Winner, Les Nuits de l'Info in Sophia Antipolis

projects.name: From question to action.
projects.description: An assistant that understands a loyalty platform, then gets things done.
projects.context: Loyalty-platform configuration means navigating complex documentation and product rules. At Amadeus, I explored how a conversational assistant could make that knowledge actionable.
projects.approach: I built the configuration-chatbot proof of concept independently: retrieval over product documentation, then a hybrid approach combining code-generated documentation and function calling.
projects.outcome: Client and prospect demos helped build support for a dedicated team, OctoMind, to take these AI use cases toward production. My work also includes Member Insight and technical documentation for the AI stack.

projects.name: Member Insight
projects.description: An agent that gives call-centre staff a grounded view of a loyalty member and recommends the next action.
projects.context: Call-centre agents need a useful picture of a member as soon as they open the record.
projects.approach: The system produces a condensed snapshot, predicts why the member may be calling with a confidence and justification, recommends a next action, and answers questions about point history. Evidence is computed deterministically in code; models handle judgement calls.
projects.outcome: Deployed to test environments behind a feature flag and developed as the OctoMind team's priority use case.

projects.name: SaaSOffice assistants
projects.description: Client-facing and internal assistants for a SaaS startup.
projects.context: The company needed assistants for visitors and staff, connected to real product workflows.
projects.approach: I built and deployed assistants for user qualification and quantitative portfolio analysis.
projects.outcome: The assistants moved applied AI into customer-facing and operational workflows.

projects.name: AI-native decision systems
projects.description: From descriptive business intelligence to world models, ontologies, and decision intelligence.
projects.context: A French-language professional thesis for the Big Data Mastère Spécialisé®, built on interviews with practitioners.
projects.approach: The work studies how decision systems can move beyond descriptive reporting through explicit knowledge and models of the world.
projects.outcome: A grounded view of AI-native decision systems and their relationship to business intelligence.

projects.name: Reality, remixed.
projects.description: Live anime style transfer. Your webcam, a neural network, and a hand sign.
projects.context: A creative experiment at the intersection of computer vision, real-time inference, and anime. What if changing a visual effect felt like casting it?
projects.approach: AnimeGANv2 transforms live webcam frames in PyTorch on Apple Silicon. MediaPipe tracks hand landmarks so Naruto-inspired hand signs can switch visual modes.
projects.outcome: A live, gesture-driven style-transfer experience that connects model inference to a playful physical interaction. This is a personal experiment, not a production product.

projects.name: A little more human.
projects.description: A portfolio with a presence. Part personal interface, part living experiment.
projects.context: A personal portfolio should feel like meeting the person behind the work. This experiment turns an authored 3D character into an interactive digital presence.
projects.approach: A rigged Three.js mascot responds to pointer movement, gestures, and a streaming conversational interface grounded in Charaf's public profile and source documents.
projects.outcome: The studio you are exploring now: an animated 3D mascot and a Python/LangGraph conversation backed by OpenAI. A clearly labelled profile preview remains available when the engine is offline.
